title: A published change to a small language model's weights leaves its default-mode math accuracy unchanged
authors: unknown (not stated in the deposited files)

headline_result.text: The published Astra edit to Qwen3.5-0.8B, rebuilt bit for bit, changed default-mode (thinking off) accuracy by 0.0 +/- 1.25 points pooled over four math benchmarks, and the unedited model in default mode already reached 74-89% of the published thinking-mode gain; in thinking mode the edit does work (49.0%).
headline_result.quote: Across them, accuracy changed by 0.0 ± 1.25 percentage points, and the unedited model in default mode already reached 74–89% of the published gain.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 1 sample per problem on MATH-500, GSM8K and Minerva, 4 on AMC23; 5 repeats per game per model for network writing

key_claims.claim: With thinking on, the published edit reproduces: 49.0% on every fifth MATH-500 problem against 45.0% published on those problems.
key_claims.quote: On every fifth MATH-500 problem, the edited model scored 49.0%, with 33% of answers cut off at the token limit; the published score on those problems was 45.0%.

key_claims.claim: The edited thinking-mode model beats the unedited default model by 4-9 points, at 5-11 times the tokens per answer.
key_claims.quote: The edited thinking-mode model beats the unedited default model by 4–9 points, at 5–11 times the tokens per answer.

key_claims.claim: A mechanical difference-of-means direction removal (no LLM) found a useful direction (17.0% vs 2.0% for a random direction) but scored about a third of the published edit.
key_claims.quote: The simple recipe therefore found a useful direction, while a random direction did nothing. The published edit nevertheless scored about three times as high as this recipe.

key_claims.claim: Zero-shot MinAtar network writing reproduced across two LLMs: 28 of 30 attempts beat the post's best 100M-step PPO baseline.
key_claims.quote: Twenty-eight of 30 attempts beat the post's best 100-million-step training baseline.

key_claims.claim: The Kinetix car edit succeeds equally on an all-zero or shuffled network, so it overrides rather than repairs the trained network.
key_claims.quote: The same edit also succeeded in every episode when applied to a network with every weight set to zero, and when applied to a network with shuffled weights.

key_claims.claim: Game identification from weights follows a row-length training footprint: a function-destroying decoy keeping only row lengths was read correctly 20 of 20 times at 96% confidence.
key_claims.quote: It also succeeded in 20 of 20 readings of a decoy that retained only the row lengths while destroying the network's function, with the same reported confidence of 96%.

limitations_stated.text: Fewer samples per problem than the original and GSM8K subsampled.
limitations_stated.quote: We used one sample per problem on MATH-500, GSM8K and Minerva and four on AMC23, whereas the post averaged two to sixteen; GSM8K used every third problem.

limitations_stated.text: Only one statistical recipe for a non-LLM edit was tested, so it is a lower bound.
limitations_stated.quote: We tested only one statistical recipe for finding an edit, so its performance is a lower bound on what such methods can achieve.

limitations_stated.text: Default and thinking modes use different token limits, and default mode still fails on a third of MATH-500 problems.
limitations_stated.quote: The comparison uses the model card's settings for each mode, including their different token limits, and default mode still fails on a third of MATH-500 problems.

notes_for_review: The sharpest critique of MIT's Experiment 8: the 7.9% baseline is the model's loop-prone optional thinking mode, and simply leaving thinking off gives 43.8% on MATH-500, so the edit's practical gain is about 4-9 points at several times the compute. It also adds a non-LLM difference-of-means edit and random-direction control, decoy tests for weight reading, and an all-zero-network control for the car repair. Evidence is single-sample on a consumer GPU at half precision, authors are not named in the deposit, and the attached (AI-style) reviews ask that 'unchanged' be framed as a measured size and note a possible folder-name leak in the original Experiment 3 runs.
